explanations.3: This tells Ubuntu to not ask interactive questions during package installation, which is necessary in Docker since there's no user to answer prompts.
explanations.5: The backslash at the end of the line lets you continue a command across multiple lines; it's purely for readability.
explanations.11: This removes the package manager's cache files to keep the Docker image smaller, since we won't need them again after installation.
explanations.14: The printf command with '%s\n' writes each quoted string on its own line; the output is redirected to create the ripgrep config file.
explanations.38: The syntax `"${1:-.}"` means 'use the first argument passed to this function, or default to the current directory if nothing was passed'.
explanations.47: This checks if the variable is empty (the -z test); if it is, the code prints usage instructions and exits the function early.
explanations.48: The `--type-add` flag teaches ripgrep about custom file types; here we're saying 'treat .env, .cfg, .ini, .conf files as the config type'.
explanations.55: This line sources (loads and runs) all the custom function files we created, making them available in the shell.
explanations.60: The double >> appends to the file instead of overwriting it, so we add these aliases to the existing .zshrc file.
explanations.79: The `-C /root/demo` tells git to run commands inside that folder without changing directories; `-q` means quiet mode.
explanations.80: The `-c` flags set git config values just for this one command; here we're providing a fake email and name for the git commit.
explanations.90: The `-i` flag runs an interactive shell and `-l` loads it as a login shell, which triggers loading all the config files we set up.
